name: John Mark
title: The Evangelist and Cousin of Barnabas
summary: John Mark was an early Christian who wrote the Gospel of Mark, the oldest of the four Gospels. He was a cousin of Barnabas and traveled companion to both Paul and Peter. Despite a difficult start to his ministry, he later became a valuable helper to the apostles.

keyEvents.title: Peter's Visit to His Mother
keyEvents.description: When Peter was miraculously freed from prison, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark, where many had gathered for prayer.

keyEvents.title: Joined the First Missionary Journey
keyEvents.description: John Mark accompanied Barnabas and Paul as a helper on their first missionary journey from Antioch.

keyEvents.title: Leaves the Missionary Journey
keyEvents.description: In Perge of Pamphylia, John Mark left Paul and Barnabas and returned to Jerusalem, which later led to conflict.

keyEvents.title: Cause of the split between Paul and Barnabas
keyEvents.description: Disagreement over John Mark caused Paul and Barnabas to part ways. Barnabas took his cousin Mark with him to Cyprus.

keyEvents.title: Reconciliation with Paul
keyEvents.description: Later, the relationship with Paul was restored. Paul refers to Mark as a valuable coworker and asks Timothy to bring him along.

keyEvents.title: Peter's 'son' in the faith
keyEvents.description: Peter calls Mark his 'son', suggesting a close spiritual relationship between them. Tradition holds that the Gospel of Mark is based on Peter's testimony.
